questions.question: In a block matrix such as $\begin{pmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{pmatrix}$, what are the symbols $A_{ij}$ meant to represent?
options: Labels for four different vector spaces.

questions.question: When can two matrices written in the same block layout be added block by block?
options: Whenever the total number of scalar entries is the same.
Only when every block is square.
When corresponding blocks have matching sizes.
Only when all off-diagonal blocks are zero.

questions.question: Why does block notation sometimes let a large matrix calculation look smaller?
options: It lets compatible submatrices be treated like larger entries.
It turns every block into a scalar number.
It changes a non-square matrix into a square matrix.
It removes the need to check dimensions.

questions.question: Before multiplying two block matrices using a row-by-column block pattern, what must be checked?
options: The two matrices must have the same number of rows.
The inner block dimensions must be compatible.
The diagonal blocks must all be zero.

questions.question: A $4\times4$ matrix is split after the second row and after the second column. How should it be viewed at the block level?
options: As a $4\times4$ block matrix with scalar blocks only.
As one block because the original matrix is square.
As a $2\times2$ block matrix with four $2\times2$ blocks.

questions.question: In $M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}$, which block is in the lower-left position?
If $\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}E&F\\G&H\end{pmatrix}$ is added blockwise, what is the upper-right block of the sum?
Suppose a block row is written as $\begin{pmatrix}A&B\end{pmatrix}$, where $A$ is $2\times3$. What must be true about $B$?
For block matrices $\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}E&F\\G&H\end{pmatrix}$, what is the $(1,2)$ block of their product?
A $3\times5$ matrix is split after row $1$ and after column $2$. What is the size of the upper-right block?
What is the most common mistake when using block notation in multiplication?
options: Forgetting that block matrices still have scalar entries inside
Treating blocks as entries without checking the products are defined
Using two block rows instead of three.
Writing zero blocks on the diagonal.

questions.question: Does writing a matrix in block form create a new matrix?
options: No, because block form is allowed only for diagonal matrices.
Yes, each block becomes an independent matrix unrelated to the original.
Yes, block form always changes the determinant.
No, it is the same matrix with a chosen partition.

questions.question: Why are submatrices the natural building pieces of block matrices?
options: Each block is always a single row.
Each block ignores the original row and column order.
Each block is a submatrix from rows and columns of the original matrix
Each block must be a determinant of the original matrix

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ and $x=\begin{pmatrix}x_1\\x_2\end{pmatrix}$. What is the first block row of $Ax$?
A $5\times5$ matrix is split into block rows of sizes $2$ and $3$, and block columns of sizes $2$ and $3$. What is the size of the lower-right block?
If $A$ is $2\times2$, $B$ is $2\times1$, $C$ is $1\times2$, and $D$ is $1\times1$, what is the size of $\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}$?
Why is it not enough for two block matrices to have the same overall size before adding them blockwise?
options: Blockwise addition works only for square matrices.
The diagonal blocks must be invertible first.
Their chosen block partitions must also match.
Overall size already forces every block size to match.

questions.question: What hidden condition is contained in the formula $(AB)_{11}=A_{11}B_{11}+A_{12}B_{21}$?
options: Both products and the final block sum must be dimensionally meaningful.
All four blocks must have the same determinant for the formula to hold

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$, $B=\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\end{pmatrix}$, and $x=\begin{pmatrix}5\\6\end{pmatrix}$, $y=7$. What is $Ax+By$?
A $6\times4$ matrix is split into block rows of sizes $1,2,3$ and block columns of sizes $3,1$. What is the size of the block in block row $2$, block column $1$?
